prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 (policy measures only)

Economy and business
- Industrial strategy focused on green infrastructure, digital and biosciences; expand British Business Bank; target 3% of GDP R&D by 2030.
- Repair EU trade relationship; seek mutual recognition and veterinary/plant health agreements; join EU programmes (e.g., Horizon, Erasmus).
- Tax changes: reverse bank tax cuts; one-off windfall tax on oil/gas; increase Digital Services Tax to 6%; reform capital gains; 4% tax on FTSE-100 buybacks.
- Abolish business rates and replace with a Commercial Landowner Levy; prompt payment enforcement; local banking network.
- Skills: replace apprenticeship levy with flexible skills levy; guarantee apprentices at least the minimum wage; £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants.
- Employment rights: create “dependent contractor” status; higher minimum wage for zero-hours at normal demand; right to fixed-hours after 12 months; SSP from day one and aligned to minimum wage; new Worker Protection Enforcement Authority.

Climate, energy and environment
- Net zero by 2045; 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030; ban fracking and new coal; decouple electricity prices from gas.
- Ten-year home upgrade (insulation, heat pumps), social energy tariff; rooftop solar expansion; community energy rights; grid and interconnector build-out.
- Carbon Border Adjustment; zero-emission vehicle sales from 2030; nationwide charging rollout and 5% VAT on public charging.
- Water: transform water companies into public benefit companies; new regulator; sewage tax; real-time discharge data; binding targets for bathing waters by 2030.
- Biodiversity: “double nature” by 2050; 60m trees/year; protect 30% land/sea by 2030; Clean Air Act and Air Quality Agency; deposit return scheme; phase-out non-recyclable single-use plastics.

Health and social care
- Right to see a GP within seven days (24 hours if urgent); 8,000 more GPs; universal 24/7 booking; expand pharmacy roles.
- NHS dentistry: urgent/emergency access, contract reform; supervised toothbrushing; remove VAT on children’s dental products.
- Mental health: hubs for young people; regular check-ups at key life stages; specialist in every school; end out-of-area placements.
- Cancer: 62-day treatment guarantee; renew radiotherapy kit; more cancer nurses; screening for high-risk prostate cancer.
- Social care: free personal care; workforce plan; Royal College of Care Workers; Carer’s Minimum Wage (+£2/hr); paid carer’s leave and guaranteed respite; National Care Agency.

Education and families
- Mental health professional in every school; per-pupil funding rise above inflation; repair unsafe buildings; tutoring guarantee for disadvantaged pupils.
- Early years: extra free hours for disadvantaged 3–4s; triple Early Years Pupil Premium; career strategy for nursery staff.
- Post-16/HE: reinstate maintenance grants; Young People’s Premium (16–18); review HE finance; return to Erasmus.
- Parental leave/pay: day-one rights incl. self-employed; double SMP/Shared Parental Pay to £350/week; 90% pay for paternity; extra month for partners; “Toddler Top-Up.”

Welfare and pensions
- Remove two-child limit and benefit cap; reduce Universal Credit wait to five days; scrap bedroom tax; replace sanctions.
- Protect triple lock; fair treatment for 1950s-born women; increase and widen Carer’s Allowance eligibility; reform disability assessments.

Crime and justice
- Restore community policing; guarantee police attendance and investigation for all burglaries.
- Online Crime Agency; replace PCCs with local Police Boards; reduce court backlogs; public health approach to youth violence.
- Modern slavery: stronger enforcement; firewall with immigration; civil redress for survivors.
- Prisons: end overcrowding; improve rehabilitation; Women’s Justice Board; Secure Schools.

Food and farming
- National Food Strategy; accelerate and fund Environmental Land Management (+£1bn); uphold high import standards; strengthen Groceries Code Adjudicator.
- EU veterinary agreement; support local abattoirs; fund alt-protein R&D; new Animal Welfare Bill, ban caged hens.

Housing and communities
- Build 380,000 homes/year including 150,000 social; 10 new garden cities; reform land compensation; use-it-or-lose-it permissions; rent-to-own model.
- Renters: ban no-fault evictions; default three-year tenancies; national landlord register.
- Abolish leasehold; cap ground rents; complete cladding remediation at no cost to leaseholders.
- Local government: multi-year settlements; controls on second homes/short-term lets; universal gigabit rollout; empower bus franchising.

Transport
- EV transition: charging rollout; restore plug-in grant; ZEV mandate from 2030.
- Rail: freeze fares; simplify ticketing; new Railway Agency; electrification and Northern Powerhouse Rail; accessibility upgrades.
- Buses: £2 fare cap while reviewed; single local fund; zero-emission fleets; active travel networks.
- Aviation: reform taxes to target frequent flyers and private jets; restrict short flights where fast rail exists; moratorium on net airport expansion.

Culture, media and sport
- Protect BBC/S4C/Alba/Channel 4; creative enterprise zones; join Creative Europe; ease EU touring for artists; Anti-SLAPP law; regulate gambling with levy, ombudsman, ad restrictions; football regulator and stronger owners’ tests.

Immigration and asylum
- End Hostile Environment; move work/student visa policy out of Home Office; scrap Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda plan; three-month asylum decision target; allow work after three months.
- Safe/legal routes: expanded resettlement, humanitarian travel permits, wider family reunion; Youth Mobility expansion; reverse raised family visa thresholds; Settled Status upgrades; repeal Right to Rent; Windrush redress.

Rights and political reform
- Uphold Human Rights Act and ECHR; Digital Bill of Rights; ban conversion practices; repeal recent anti-protest laws; pause live facial recognition.
- PR (STV) for MPs and English councillors; scrap voter ID; votes at 16; cap donations; legislate Ministerial Code; Lords reform; citizens’ assemblies; transparency on lobbying and ministerial messaging.

Defence and international
- Increase defence spending towards 2.5% of GDP; reverse Army cuts; maintain nuclear deterrent; parliamentary vote before military action (with emergency provision).
- EU security cooperation; support Ukraine including using seized Russian assets; restore aid to 0.7% GNI via independent department.
- Middle East: immediate ceasefire in Israel-Gaza, recognise Palestine, pursue two-state solution; sanction human rights abuses; protect consular rights.
